P1.evidence: The application was acknowledged but not read back — "I seen your application uh that you sent to us so uh I have just a few information" — so nothing was reflected that would make him feel seen. The frame was one part of four: "what I would like to do is just to have a chat with you and go through everything, like in detail and actually assess if we are the ones that can help you." No where-you-are / where-you-want-to-go / what's-in-the-way / what-you-need structure, and no explicit "does that work?" — he took "Okay. Perfect." as agreement. The open question ran cleanly: "what's been going on? Like, what's the main thing you're trying to fix right now?"

P2.evidence: Five of nine run properly and asked directly: "how old are you right now?", "what's your height?", "how much do you weigh currently?", "when you're running a business, is it more that you're sitting all day or what does it look like?", "any injuries or anything that limits your movement", "What are you actually doing right now in terms of fitness?", and "the big nutrition part how does it look like for you right now" followed by "walk me through like, what's your typical day?" The injury probe was genuinely good — it surfaced eight years of wrist history and that he had never had it assessed. The misses matter though: health conditions own or hereditary were never asked at all, results from current training were never asked, energy was never asked, and sleep was never asked despite the prospect volunteering that a 15-month-old sleeps in his bed and he no longer wakes early.

P3.evidence: The strongest phase in the batch. The one-thing question ran ("Is there any particular weight that you would like to hit?") and got leanness and love handles. The bridge ran verbatim: "what would be your, so to say, like your big why? Why do you want to do this?" The future-possibility question ran: "when you hit your goals in those six months... what's becoming more possible that it wasn't possible? What new opportunities show up?" The can't-do-now question ran and surfaced kiteboarding. The impact drove all the way through to five children, the energy gap between his first three and his youngest two, and the family trips. And the reflect-back ran twice with tie-downs: "we're playing here the long-term game of longevity, not just the aesthetic", and later "you're not lacking commitment and showing up. It's just that with your busy schedule... it's difficult for you to follow anything" → "Correct." Only P3b is soft — the mobility/strength/energy menu was asserted rather than offered.

P4.evidence: "Why haven't you fixed it before?" got the answer the phase exists to produce: "I think it's structure, accountability." The one-thing-in-the-way was then landed and confirmed in the reflect-back. The prospect named the gap himself and at length — "when you don't have a clear plan that you know it's gonna work... I lose motivation" and "I want a plan that I feel that can work." What was thin: the past-attempts inventory was not really taken, the vegan year came up in passing and was not unpacked, and the "information isn't the problem" line was never run even though the prospect handed it over — "I understand the science behind it. I've done my research."

P5.evidence: Not run. No two-year question, no settling question, no why-not, no line in the sand. The rep worked the opposite direction throughout — future-positive rather than cost-of-inaction. The only fragments are two early throwaways: "the growth doesn't happen from being comfortable right" and "stagnation means uh you're declining basically." This is the third call of the day from this rep with no consequence frame, and it is the phase he needed when the prospect asked for twenty-four hours.

P6.evidence: Both questions ran. The all-in check came before the price, correctly placed: "the most important question I want to ask you before we move further, if we can figure out all the details are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become that version 2.0 of Alex?" → "yeah yeah yeah". The belief question ran later as an objection move: "from what you saw in the videos and testimonials and everything, do you actually feel that this can get you to your goals?" → "Yeah. Yeah. I think so." P6c fails on the second half of the check: when hesitation surfaced after the price, the script says return to Phase 5. There was no Phase 5 to return to, so the rep returned to price instead and cut a new structure.

P11.evidence: Executed more completely than anything else in this batch, across the main call and the continuation recording. Payment collected — "so the payment went through." Trevor onboarding booked for 5:45pm the next day with a confirmation sent, and the rep checked receipt: "You should get confirmation about the onboarding session with Trevor, let me know when you have it." The welcome material was covered: agreement, onboarding form to complete before the Trevor call, and the Skool community link, with the rep confirming Skool is included at no extra cost. The one deviation is the signature — the script says sign it on the call, the rep deferred it: "just remember to sign the agreement when you have time, somewhat in the afternoon today."

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran, correctly worded and at the right moment: "Finances aside, like, there is, are you sure, like, there's nothing else keeping you from being 100%?" The upfront norm ran: "most of the guys just put it on a credit card and handle it in one sitting. Why would you ask?" Payment structures were offered. But the play's actual substance — the financial picture — was never opened. Not one of the six questions ran: cash on hand, what is left over each month after bills, how many credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, crypto or stocks or investments. Nor did the "you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place" reframe. Without the financial picture the rep had no basis for deciding what this prospect could carry, so he solved for the objection by cutting the commitment instead — which is the opposite of what the play is for.

"give me like 24 hours or 12 hours like to tomorrow to make a decision" and "I normally like to give it some thought process before I make a final decision." Two scripted moves ran: the belief question — "do you actually feel that this can get you to your goals?" → "Yeah. Yeah. I think so." — and a variant of the what's-actually-preventing-you probe: "what would be the reason that you wouldn't start right away." The rest did not: no "thinking isn't the problem, deciding is", no "the way you've been approaching this brought you here", no identity move, no final "are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?" The objection was ultimately closed by changing the price and the term rather than by the play.

Real fear and trust doubt, stated plainly: "I don't want to get hurt either and lose the money", "this is all new to me", "I've never even done a personal trainer. I've never done a coaching before", and a direct probe on whether Trevor uses drugs. The rep diagnosed it well — "Is it that you're not sure how Trevor works with people and that gets you like in a hesitant state?" — and answered with the written strength guarantee and the injury-pause policy, which is substantive. None of the scripted moves ran, and the burned-before move was left on the table when the prospect volunteered exactly that story unprompted: "I've had people work for me for a year or two that I thought were different people... doing things that you never think they would do." That was the moment for it.

The prospect pre-empted the objection and half-disclaimed it: "I don't want to be the typical guy says I'm gonna talk to my wife right and let you get back", then "I do you know speak to her about things and kind of get her input on it but ultimately that's not going to be it's my decision." The rep ran a compressed version of the responsibility move — "you're a business owner you don't need to talk to your wife right" — which landed, but skipped the softer scripted framing ("Is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain?", "This isn't a joint decision like buying a house").

Script gap worth recording. This is a first-time coaching buyer — he has never hired a trainer or bought anything online like this — asking for a smaller first commitment rather than disputing value or capacity: "If it was a commitment right now to start even monthly, you know, where I can work at it." The playbook has no play for it, and the rep filled the gap by inventing a one-month tier and an opt-out that do not exist in the offer. A second unscripted trigger sits alongside it: a direct risk-of-harm question, "in the injuries, are they caused by the kettlebell workouts?", answered with an unsupported modality-safety claim rather than any screening process.

notes: Textbook discovery and a nearly complete P11 wrapped around a missing P5 and an improvised close. The single highest-value coaching point is that skipping the consequence frame cost him the leverage he needed forty minutes later — with no cost of inaction established, the only currency left when the prospect hesitated was price, and he spent it. Second point: he asked the injury question well enough to learn the wrist had never been medically assessed, and then reassured rather than screened.
